Whether it is a **duty disability benefit** or an **ordinary disability benefit** depends on whether the injury was incurred while performing an act or acts of duty.

- A duty disability benefit applies if the injury occurred in the performance of an act or acts of duty, while you were under age 70 and receiving no salary. [40 ILCS 5/11-155]

turns.question: i am an employee of a board of park commissioners, how is my pension calculated?
turns.answer:
Under Article 12, the fixed-benefit formula is **2.40% for each year of credited service**, based on your highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years before you leave service. The annuity is capped at 80% of that average salary. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

A figure cannot be given until your fund corrects your record from Article 11 to Article 12. The Article 11 salary, service, and averages on file are not the right basis here.

The formula applies if you leave service on or after December 31, 2003, at age 50 or over with at least 10 years of service, or at age 60 or over with at least 4 years of service. If you retire before age 60, the annuity is reduced by 1/4 of 1% for each month or fraction of a month before age 60, unless you are age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133(a)]

To put a figure to your pension, the fund would need your age when you leave service, your credited service—including any prorated service for less than a full year—your highest average annual salary for 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years, and your date of birth to determine any months before age 60. The Code provides that a retirement annuity consists of a service annuity and a prior service annuity where applicable. [40 ILCS 5/12-128]

The earlier fixed-benefit rates do not apply because they cover withdrawals before December 31, 2003. The accumulation-based option in Section 12-133(b) applies only to an employee in service before July 1, 1971. Section 12-130 likewise does not apply to this calculation because its accumulation-based amount is limited to an employee who entered service before July 1, 1971. [40 ILCS 5/12-133] [40 ILCS 5/12-130]

Your fund owns the correction of your coverage record and the Article 12 pension figures; the Code does not determine that administrative correction here.

turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 sets minimum annuity formulas based on your years of service and highest average salary. The applicable formula depends on your withdrawal date, age, and service credit.

- For qualifying employees with at least 20 years of service, the section provides tiered formulas based on service years and the highest average annual salary for 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years.
- An employee who withdraws before age 60 may have the annuity reduced for each month or fractional month that the annuity begins before age 60. The section also provides exceptions for certain employees with at least 25 or 30 years of service.
- Employees with at least 20 years of service may elect another formula that uses a rate for each year of service, subject to the applicable age-reduction rules and maximum annuity limits.
- Section 11-134 also provides an election for employees with at least 10 years of service to receive a retirement annuity beginning no earlier than age 60, using final average salary and a service-based formula.
- The annuity is paid in equal monthly installments. [40 ILCS 5/11-134(g)]

Your record shows age 56 and 21.5 years of service, so the section's provisions for employees with at least 20 years of service reach you. A dollar amount cannot be worked out here because no benefit figure was calculated this turn; the amount would require applying the selected statutory formula to your salary basis and the applicable withdrawal and annuity-start dates.



**What I assumed**

- the date you stop working, taken as today

turns.question: Using my employee record, determine my governing Article and my current pension status. Do not calculate anything yet.
turns.answer:
Your record places you in Article 11, and your current pension status is active. You have not withdrawn from service or begun receiving a retirement annuity.

- Article 11 covers the annuity and benefit fund whose service-credit and minimum-annuity rules appear in Sections 11-215, 11-216, and 11-134. [40 ILCS 5/11-215] [40 ILCS 5/11-216]
- Because you are recorded as active, retirement provisions that require withdrawal from service do not yet establish a payable retirement annuity. Section 11-134 applies its minimum-annuity rules when an employee withdraws from service and meets the stated age and service conditions. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- No pension amount is being determined here. To work one out later, the record would also need your intended withdrawal date and the retirement annuity option you elect, because Article 11 provides more than one election in qualifying circumstances.

**What I assumed**

turns.question: Identify every retirement pathway that could potentially apply to me.
turns.answer:
You have several potential Article 11 retirement pathways. Because your record shows you are active, none is payable until you withdraw from service.

- **Withdrawal at age 55 but before age 60:** With at least 10 years of service, Section 11-130 provides an age-and-service annuity. [40 ILCS 5/11-130]
- **Minimum annuity:** Because your record shows Tier 1, 21.5 years of service, and age 56, the minimum-annuity provisions may apply when you withdraw. Section 11-134 also gives qualifying employees with at least 20 years of service an election among certain lifetime annuity options. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- **Withdrawal before age 55 after leaving service:** This does not fit your current age, but Section 11-131 applies when an employee withdraws before age 55 after at least 10 years of service and later reaches age 55. [40 ILCS 5/11-131]
- **Withdrawal at age 60 but before age 65:** Section 11-129 provides another age-and-service pathway for an employee who withdraws in that age range. [40 ILCS 5/11-129]
- **Withdrawal at or after age 65:** Section 11-134 includes additional minimum-annuity provisions for certain employees with at least 15 years of service, and separate provisions for some employees with fewer than 20 years. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

To work out a benefit figure, I would need your intended withdrawal date and the annuity option you would elect, because the applicable pathway and any election depend on those facts. Your final average salary and months before age 60 are already listed, but I will not turn them into a figure here.

**What I assumed**

- the date you stop working, taken as today

- **Withdrawal at age 55 but before age 60:** Your age is 56, and your record shows 21.5 years of service. Those facts meet the age and service conditions described for the pathway. Your withdrawal from service is still required. - **Minimum annuity under Section 11-134:** Your record shows age 56 and 21.5 years of service. The provision requires withdrawal after age 55 and at least 20 years of service for the applicable early-retirement options. It also requires that the annuity begin no earlier than age 55. Your record meets those age and service thresholds, but the annuity cannot begin while you remain active. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- **Section 11-134 election:** Section 11-134 provides qualifying employees with a choice among specified annuity formulas. That choice is yours. The record shows the age and service needed to reach the 20-year threshold, but the provision also requires withdrawal from service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your record does not state that you are disabled, so eligibility cannot be established from the listed data. Duty disability requires a qualifying injury incurred in the performance of an act or acts of duty. Ordinary disability requires a qualifying disability and is not a retirement annuity. [40 ILCS 5/11-155] [40 ILCS 5/11-156]

turns.question: Which were the strongest competitors, and why did you accept one and reject the others?
turns.answer:
The strongest competitors are the age-and-service annuity under Section 11-130 and the minimum-annuity elections under Section 11-134. The accepted pathway is not yet a payable pension because your record shows you are still active; withdrawal from service is required.

- Section 11-130 reaches an employee age 55 or more but less than 60 with at least 10 years of service. Your record shows age 56 and 21.5 years of service, so that pathway reaches you. Its amount cannot be worked out here because the statute requires the accumulated annuity credits and the applicable employee and city contributions. [40 ILCS 5/11-130]
- Section 11-134 also reaches you because it covers withdrawal at age 60 or over with at least 20 years of service, and it provides separate elections for employees with at least 20 years of service who withdraw before age 60. Those elections are your choice; they are not rejected merely because another provision is available. The record does not contain the withdrawal date or enough information to determine which election would provide the larger result. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- Section 11-131 is not applicable because it concerns an employee who withdraws before age 55 and later attains age 55 while out of service; your record shows age 56 and active employment. [40 ILCS 5/11-131]
- Sections 11-141 and 11-143 concern a widow's annuity, not your own retirement annuity, so they are not the governing pathway for your pension. [40 ILCS 5/11-141] [40 ILCS 5/11-143]

To work out a pension figure, the record would need your intended withdrawal date, the accumulated age-and-service and city-contribution credits required under Section 11-130, and confirmation of which Section 11-134 election you want compared.

- the date you stop working, taken as today
